channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: Tehran will not surrender in war with U.S., but believes in diplomacy: Iran President tells UN
item.description: President Masoud Pezeshkian held up photos of the late Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and the more than 150 school children killed on the first days of the war; The ‌United States delegation walked out ‌at ⁠the start of the speech Tehran will not surrender in war with U. S., but believes in diplomacy: Iran President tells UN.

item.title: Five Afghan Family Members Die Of Thirst While Trying To Reach Iran
item.description: An Afghan migrant reported that his stepmother and four sisters died An Afghan migrant has told RFE/RL's Radio Azadi that his stepmother and four sisters died of thirst and hunger while attempting a dangerous journey to Iran after economic hardship forced the family to leave Afghanistan again. Five Afghan Family Members Die Of Thirst While Trying To Reach Iran.

item.title: Delcy Rodríguez poses with Trump in New York as Maduro languishes in jail nearby
item.description: Venezuela’s interim president hails ‘historic meeting’ and does not say whether she will visit snatched predecessorVenezuela’s interim president, Delcy Rodríguez, has celebrated a “historic” meeting with Donald Trump in New York, posing for a smiley photo with the US president, less than nine months after he ordered the abduction of her boss, Nicolás Maduro. Delcy Rodríguez poses with Trump in New York as Maduro languishes in jail nearby.

item.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak toll exceeds 3,700 deaths
item.description: More than 130 days into the latest Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), health experts said on Wednesday that response efforts have been scaled up significantly and “the first encouraging signs of progress” are now being seen. DR Congo Ebola outbreak toll exceeds 3,700 deaths.

item.title: US Set To Unveil Next Steps for Trump-Backed Armenia-Azerbaijan Transit Corridor
item.description: The United States is set to unveil the next stage of TRIPP, a planned transport corridor through southern Armenia that Washington says could open new trade routes linking the South Caucasus and Central Asia with Western markets. US Set To Unveil Next Steps for Trump-Backed Armenia-Azerbaijan Transit Corridor.

item.title: ‘Super El Niño’ projected to cause 15,800 additional heat deaths in India, says report
item.description: The heaviest toll is expected in poorer countries, already struggling with food insecurity and high energy costs, partly due to climate change and the fallout of the war in Iran, the University of Chicago-based Climate Impact Lab says This year’s El Niño-driven heat could cause nearly half a million more deaths, group says. ‘This year’s El Niño is also a ‘postcard from our future’, bringing temperatures climate change is projected to deliver 20 years in the future.

item.title: Iranian Hard-Liners Up In Arms After Araqchi-Witkoff Meeting In New York
item.description: Iranian hard‑liners condemned the meeting between US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi in New York on US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi met in New York on September 22 following days of signals that US-Iranian talks would take place on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. The meeting sparked a backlash from Iranian hard-liners.

item.title: Amid Setbacks In The Sahel, Russia Quietly And Quickly Builds Ties In Madagascar
item.description: Russia’s efforts to cultivate clout in Africa’s Sahel have been a mixed bag of successes and setbacks. Across the continent, however, on the Indian Ocean island of Madagascar, Moscow is making another quiet push for influence. Amid Setbacks In The Sahel, Russia Quietly And Quickly Builds Ties In Madagascar.

item.title: Why China’s Silicon Valley won’t need American degrees
item.description: For nearly a century, American global power has rested on a three-legged tripod: unmatched military firepower, the ubiquitous sovereignty of the US dollar and the intellectual dominance of its higher-education system. While aircraft carriers project hard power and Wall Street manages global capital, the American university system has quietly manufactured the “soft power,” technological breakthroug Why China’s Silicon Valley won’t need American degrees.

item.title: Time to recognize the Houthis as Yemen’s real government
item.description: The Trump administration came perilously close to launching another bombing campaign against Yemen this weekend. According to a September 20 New York Times report, US commanders had approved their targets, American troops were loading bombs onto warplanes, and an attack on Yemen’s Ansar Allah forces was about to begin when President Donald Trump abruptly reversed course. For two weeks, Saudi Crown.

item.title: Jamaica hails King’s decision to refer slavery reparations petition to privy council as ‘really big
item.description: The move comes after Jamaica’s culture minister Olivia Grange travelled to the UK earlier this month to lodge the historic petitionKing Charles has referred a landmark slavery reparations petition from Jamaica to a high-level UK appeals court for legal advice, Jamaica’s culture minister announced in parliament on Tuesday. Jamaica hails King’s decision to refer slavery reparations petition to privy council as ‘really big.

item.title: Trump, Zelenskyy Discuss Peace Negotiations, Potential Energy Cease-Fire
item.description: US President Donald Trump met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. Trump said he believes that both sides "want to see the war end." Zelenskyy said Ukraine is pushing for an agreement with Russia on halting attacks on energy infrastructure. Trump, Zelenskyy Discuss Peace Negotiations, Potential Energy Cease-Fire.

item.title: Trump’s threat to annihilate Iran to UN general assembly is stunning, even for him
item.description: US president may have upstaged the ghost of Soviet leader Khrushchev by musing destruction of fellow member stateDonald Trump has a habit of discomfiting delegates to the United Nations general assembly. But this year, he may have upstaged the ghost of former Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev by openly contemplating the annihilation of a fellow UN member state. Trump’s threat to annihilate Iran to UN general assembly is stunning, even for him.

item.title: Why Saudi Arabia’s Oil Is Getting Harder To Ship
item.description: The crises in the Middle East are creating a growing challenge for Saudi Arabia: how it gets its oil to global markets. Shipping costs are rising, oil has topped $105 a barrel, and global inventories are being rapidly drained. Why Saudi Arabia’s Oil Is Getting Harder To Ship.

item.title: Children demand a voice on AI’s future
item.description: The first generation to grow up with AI may also be the last one anyone thinks to ask about it – and that has to change, the UN's top human rights official said on Tuesday. Children demand a voice on AI’s future.

item.title: UN rendered unable to fulfil its mission, Turkish President laments before world leaders
item.description: The United Nations continues to be weakened, and those who have tied their hopes to the world body – from Palestine to Sudan – have been disappointed, Türkiye’s President said, while adding that his country is committed to restoring confidence in the Organization. UN rendered unable to fulfil its mission, Turkish President laments before world leaders.

item.title: Trump defends military action against Iran, Venezuela, and calls for rebrand of AI
item.description: US President Donald Trump used his address to the UN General Assembly on Tuesday to defend recent military action against Iran, urging countries to maintain economic pressure on Tehran – and declaring that he now faces a choice between making a deal, or taking far more drastic steps. Trump defends military action against Iran, Venezuela, and calls for rebrand of AI.

item.title: Diplomacy is the way to address global challenges, Brazil tells General Assembly
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva told the General Assembly on Tuesday that the UN needs to become a “temple of peace” once again, as it confronts one of the most critical periods in its 80-year history. Diplomacy is the way to address global challenges, Brazil tells General Assembly.

item.title: Time to accept ‘hard truths’ so trust can be rebuilt: General Assembly President
item.description: The UN’s survival for 80 years is not, by itself, proof of success, and now, the institution must confront painful truths if it hopes to rebuild public trust, said Khalilur Rahman, president of the General Assembly’s 81st session on Tuesday. Time to accept ‘hard truths’ so trust can be rebuilt: General Assembly president.

item.title: ‘Cracks have become canyons’ as world faces four tests of power
item.description: Humanity faces four defining “tests of power” – around war or peace, inequality, climate change and AI – that will determine whether the world moves towards a new era of cooperation or deeper division, the UN chief warned the General Assembly on Tuesday. ‘Cracks have become canyons’ as world faces four tests of power.
